Auto-summary: quick tuning session to align on batcher scheduler knobs and pilot plan; some transcript artefacts expected.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick roll call?
[00:06] Tom: hey tom here, maya and rory on as well. excited to tune this — we've been hitting some weird p90 spikes.
[00:12] Alex: awesome. priya and jordan are with me - priya will lead the deep dive on the scheduler and continuous batching.
[00:20] Priya: hi all. yeah, goal is to get to the root of p90/p99 variability and then propose a small set of knobs you can test in the pilot. i'll try to keep it concrete with configs.

[02:10] Priya: quick context check: you're running a mix of short chat prompts and long generation with token limits around 1024, is that right?
[02:18] Rory: correct. about 60% short (<=50 tokens), 40% long (200-800), and peak QPS around 120 requests/sec across their service.
[02:25] Priya: ok that explains a lot. continuous batching works best when sequence length distribution is predictable, otherwise the scheduler ends up waiting for long queries which inflates latency for short ones.

[05:03] Jordan: a couple terms i'll use: max_num_seqs — max sequences per batch, batch_time_ms — how long scheduler waits to fill; also the dynamic token-aware scheduler we use can preempt/early-flush if long seqs would cause latency SLO misses.
[05:18] Tom: is dynamic token-aware scheduler on by default in hosted? what about Dedicated?
[05:22] Priya: hosted defaults to conservative settings optimized for mixed workloads; Dedicated gives you access to lower-level knobs (max_num_seqs, per-worker batch_time_ms, continuous_batching_enabled flags). you can flip the dynamic token-aware behavior too.

[07:00] Rory: we're trying Dedicated because of isolation, but we don't want to blow up ops to tune everything. can you suggest safe starting values?
[07:08] Priya: yes — safe starter: continuous_batching_enabled=true, max_num_seqs=16 for your GPU type (A10/A100 mix), batch_time_ms=15-25 (start high if you care about throughput), token_limit_per_batch=2048. that gives good batches without too much p99 tail impact.

[09:40] Maya: quick Q — what's the interplay with KV cache? we do heavy chat with long contexts and rely on KV for fast prefix.
[09:47] Priya: key point: KV cache reduces per-token compute but increases memory footprint and can affect batch packing because cached prefixes mean a lot of sequences with long total context but small incremental generation. scheduler should treat cached prefix length vs generated tokens differently — our token-aware scheduler natively accounts for generation tokens so you don't overpack.
[10:10] Alex: in practice that means you might cap max_total_tokens_in_batch lower if many requests have huge prefixes, or rely on our prefix cache hints to the scheduler.

[12:30] Priya: want to show a simple synthetic: if you have 80% short requests, 20% long, naive batching with max_num_seqs=64 will create huge variance; switching to max_num_seqs=16 with batch_time_ms=20 shrinks p95 by ~35% in our bench.
[12:50] Rory: do you have that bench sheet?
[12:52] Priya: yes, i'll share link after call — "redwood/tuning/throughput-bench-2026-03" (note: link shared in chat).

[15:05] Tom: what about token limits — we set per-request token max at 1024 but seen requests that go to 2k occasionally. does the scheduler reject or split?
[15:15] Jordan: we don't split requests automatically; you can set token_limit_per_request to guard against runaway jobs. for long generations we recommend streaming and setting max_new_tokens; also the kv cache hinting helps avoid re-sending large prefixes.

[17:40] Priya: quantization notes: going from FP16 to 4-bit quant improves throughput per GPU but increases variance for certain attention ops; for throughput-focused workloads we recommend 8-bit or our tuned 4-bit profiles that we verify per-model. there is a small latency increase on the first token due to dequantization and kernel selection.
[18:10] Rory: would quant cause correctness/regression risk? we need to pass QA.
[18:20] Priya: there's always a small risk—we do per-model accuracy checks and can recommend AB tests; Redwood Optimize also flags quality regressions on eval prompts.

[20:30] Tom: on VPC/on-prem: if we move to private, do we still get the same scheduler knobs?
[20:38] Alex: yes, Private gives you the same runtime controls; on-prem package includes the tuning scripts and metrics exporters. only the default policies differ — you manage autoscaler configs yourself.

[22:55] Priya: one subtlety — on-prem networking can affect scheduling if you're using multi-host KV shards; latency between hosts increases KV read time which can bump per-token latency; factor that in when you size nodes.

[25:00] Rory: what's the guidance for max_num_seqs per GPU? e.g. A100 80GB vs A10?
[25:08] Jordan: rule of thumb: A100 can handle larger max_num_seqs (32-64) for short models; A10 you're safer at 8-16. but this depends on seq length and quantization. also watch aggregate tokens per batch more than seq count: 32 short seqs can be fine, 16 long seqs not.

[28:10] Priya: also consider token-limited batching: instead of max_num_seqs, set max_tokens_per_batch=4096-8192; scheduler will pack variable-length sequences more efficiently. for mixed workloads, token-limited batching typically achieves better throughput and more predictable latency.

[31:00] Maya: we saw p90 jumps during sudden traffic spikes — is there an autoscale interplay?
[31:08] Alex: yes; initial traffic spike causes new workers to spin up, during that warm-up your p90 can spike. we recommend overprovisioning a small buffer and using burst capacity to handle spikes, plus sticky routing during scale events.

[33:40] Priya: demoing a short config change: toggling continuous_batching_enabled=false reduces throughput but flattens tail; enabling it with smaller max_num_seqs and token limits gives better tokens/sec.
[34:05] Rory: can we do an A/B between continuous on vs off?
[34:10] Priya: yes — we can route 10% traffic to the new config and compare p50/p95/p99. we have rollout tooling in the console.

[36:50] Tom: curious about cost delta — how much cheaper is it to push for higher batching vs using more GPUs?
[36:58] Jordan: batching increases utilization and lowers cost per token; but it trades latency. generally if you can accept slightly higher p95, batching wins on $/token. we can model your workload and show expected dollars/token for a few profiles.

[39:30] Maya: any gotchas with streaming responses and batching? some of our clients expect immediate partial tokens.
[39:40] Priya: streaming works with continuous batching; the scheduler may prioritize short responses to reduce time-to-first-token. you can enable low-latency preempt queues for streaming endpoints, that will take priority over high-throughput batches.

[41:55] Rory: about metrics — what should we collect from our side to make tuning easier?
[42:02] Priya: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, batch_size_distribution, token_count_per_request, KV cache hit ratio, per-worker GPU utilization, and queue_time_ms. if you share those logs we can suggest tuned values.

[44:20] Tom: ok, sounds actionable. what's the pilot look like?
[44:24] Alex: quick pilot: 3-node Dedicated pool, start with continuous_batching_enabled=true, max_num_seqs=16, max_tokens_per_batch=8192, batch_time_ms=20; run for 48 hours under representative load; collect above metrics.

[46:00] Rory: timeline?
[46:05] Alex: we aim to kick off 2026-03-09 and have initial results 2026-03-13. priya will provide configs and a reproduce script.

[48:30] Maya: can you also include sample observability dashboards?
[48:35] Jordan: yes — we'll share the console dashboard link and a Grafana export.

[50:10] Tom: one more question — what about fallback during overloads? we don't want user-facing failures.
[50:16] Priya: Redwood supports policy-based fallback: degrade to smaller model, fall back to cached completions, or return a degraded response. you can configure automatic fallback thresholds based on queue_time_ms and error rate.

[52:40] Rory: sweet. any compliance or security concerns for Dedicated?
[52:46] Alex: Dedicated plus Private options support SOC2/ISO controls, RBAC, KMS integration; full security pack is available for enterprise customers. we'll include the security deck.

[54:05] Tom: recap and next steps?
[54:10] Alex: recap: we'll share tuning guide, scheduler config, bench sheet, and observability exports; you (Arbor) will run pilot on 3-node Dedicated and share logs; schedule pilot kickoff for 2026-03-09. action items and owners are in chat.
[54:30] Maya: thanks all, appreciate the concrete steps.
[54:35] Alex: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links.
